connection_type: I have direct personal experience (as an immigrant, refugee, religious minority, or member of a marginalised group)
disclosure_text: I immigrated to the US with my family 28 years old as a young teen. In those 28 years I have encounter many hardships such as racism, prejudice and many many other obstacles as a person of color.
micronarrative: Growing up, I felt like an outsider, being an immigrant from another country.  People would give me those sideways glances, assuming I was here illegally, and I heard the phrase "go back to your country" more times than I can count. It was a constant reminder that despite my legal status, I was still seen as an outsider. At home, I spoke my native language, a small comfort in a world that often felt hostile. But everywhere else, I had to switch to English, a language that, while familiar, was not my first. The protests and the shouts of "immigrants are taking jobs" were a stark reality, even though I was already a US citizen. Those moments were painful, a constant battle to prove my belonging in a country that often doubted it.
